title: Prove exact local costs for residue-corank-one targets (no new κ)
body:
## Summary

Scoped algebraic proof: every n-role target over a central local K-algebra whose residue has division-algebra rank n-1 attains the paid right-vector column lower bound, including singular endpoints.

```text
E = {v in K^n : Mv belongs to K^n}
cost(M) = delta(M) = n - dim_K M(E) <= n
delta(M) = min_{T in GL_n(K)} dim_K ((MT-I)K^n)

Fix independent base-field images by free charts.
Choose unit pivots through the penultimate column.
Replace the final column without inverting the singular endpoint.
```

Paid factors are I+u y^T with y over K; arbitrary free GL_n(K) maps are allowed anywhere. The residue division algebra may be larger than K or noncommutative. The proof assumes neither finite dimension nor a nilpotent radical. It supplies an attaining word with no auxiliary roles. Only the six files in `research/local-corank-one-cost/` are added. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit ToikY #4334 for the singular-target gap; Nick Petalas #4276/#4243/#4787 for predecessor criteria, column bounds and local constructions; Wentao Li #4099 following #2513 for the alphabet and column-bound lineage. Basis extension, Gaussian elimination, Schur complements and local-ring unit lifting retain classical credit. The predecessor results are cited, not audited.

## Evidence

- Before: #4276 covers unit-entry local targets on two roles; #4787 covers invertible local targets at arbitrary role count. After: PROOF.md handles residue-corank-one singular endpoints at every role count. The singular fixed-space formula counts M(E), rather than E: diag(1,1,0) has E=K^3 and exact cost one.
- The self-contained standard-library verifier checks 1,112 three/four-role targets across binary and ternary dual numbers, a binary two-generator square-zero algebra, F4 over F2 and noncommutative F4[e;Frobenius]/e^2 over F2. The binary dual-number domain includes all 512 lifts of diag(1,1,0); the other domains are explicitly bounded samples. Every literal paid word and all 8,272 basis-data executions pass.
- All 5,376 direct chart evaluations pass: every one of the 168 GL3(F2) charts is evaluated on each of 32 selected targets, independently comparing the definition of delta to the constructed cost. Eight domain/word rejection controls pass. Two additional shared two-role targets over F4[e]/e^2 have costs one and two, as detailed below. No predecessor census is rerun.
- Both warning-strict registered commands pass locally. They were timed separately at 0.269 s ordinary and 0.268 s optimized. Complete generated receipts agree and bind all six package files. The registered package runner passes.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight passes at `da6f858f21d407648a711d8fd369c37a9c6df24e`. Official committed export integrity and optimized direct replay from a read-only Git-free export with PATH=/nonexistent pass with an identical generated receipt. In-memory compilation and staged whitespace checks pass. No receipt is handwritten.

Exact reproduction from the repository root, using CPython 3.12 and its standard library:


Any CPython 3.12 path may replace the displayed local path. Expected markers are `PASS_LOCAL_CORANK_ONE_COST targets=1112 controls=8 no_new_kappa`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`.

Canonical main is pinned at `624de9dc66858af0945e5f8a0942488d62280d43`, priority revision 7, fetched again before committing. The formal-interface card is explicitly changed to this algebraic side question. Its historical baseline command stops with `KeyError: 'bit_lower'` under the changed selected schema; no baseline pass is claimed. Live claims/open bodies, distinctive main README terms and merged searches were refreshed before committing. The broader overlap helper covered 325 open PRs and 3,742 Discussion records with complete remote pagination; sparse local-note coverage was incomplete. These searches do not certify novelty.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19132023).

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The universal claim rests on the written scoped proof. The finite checks cover only the specified rings and bounded domains. Residue corank at least two and nonlocal algebras are outside the cost theorem. Physical coefficient preparation, frames, routing, restoration, precision, stock and a complete recursive invoice remain unknown. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed. Lean, Docker and the selected operator replay were not run. Every registered package command ran locally.

## Open next questions

- Characterize which residue-corank-two local targets attain delta. Begin with one three-role target over F2[x,y]/(x,y)^2 with residue diag(1,0,0). A nonunit intermediate pivot needs a new completion argument.
- Specify one native dirty-input/output contract for a singular column factor and price preparation, frames, movement and restoration before using it in a supplier.

## Related open work

- #4787, head `4b58e8cd5690bd35cf01b0018eefa2c39a298920`, proves arbitrary-role invertible local costs. This theorem requires residue corank exactly one, so endpoint domains and sampled cost counts are disjoint. Its construction and credit are retained as predecessors.
- #4781, head `b838121c65e1bfd17a65466c95940eb00f12a225`, counts two-role rank-one residue lifts over proper field extensions. Its targets satisfy this theorem at n=2. A literal shared check over F4[e]/e^2 over F2 gives cost one for diag(1,e), whose nonzero base-field image space has dimension one, and cost two for [[1,e],[e,0]], whose such image space is zero. These agree with its one-factor line criterion. Its full lift totals are cited, not rechecked or extended here.
- #4780, head `a4436fab4164eccc498d4d9885eec68211c869de`, studies singular rank-one tuples over field products. Multiple components are nonlocal and outside this theorem. At the single-field boundary a separate literal check gives cost one for the shared binary projection diag(1,0), agreeing with its one-component law. No multi-component threshold or population is compared to our samples.
- #4776, head `0764ab259a8ce496a4c5d4debeed4c4e4d9f7ca4`, classifies zero-residue square-zero pencils. For n>=2 those have residue corank n, so they are outside this theorem. At n=1 a separate literal check gives exact cost one for both x and x+y over the binary two-generator square-zero algebra, agreeing with both statements. No pencil census overlaps these samples.
- #4789, head `7fdbf8040ea9a957af0576067df2d9cb6fcf0e51`, classifies two-role ordinary rank-two targets over M_m(K), m>=3. Those matrix algebras are nonlocal; no exact-cost census or target domain overlaps.
- #4784, head `4d0a6363fe4f45dd9a769f5b74d02fc5d9061ae3`, counts invertible polynomial-matrix costs over F_q[t]. That coefficient ring is nonlocal and those endpoints are invertible; no cost distribution or target count overlaps.

### Related open work refresh before DONE

This account's open PRs created since the CLAIM at 2026-10-22T20:12:38Z were listed before DONE. The four additional same-alphabet titles and bodies were read:

- #4805, head `fbf2bd033f2d3ae1605a3cad690e1fc2fbf477e7`, proves a three-factor upper bound for all two-role targets over full matrix algebras. Those algebras are nonlocal for block size at least two. At the shared scalar-block boundary, a fresh literal check gives cost one for the binary projection diag(1,0), compatible with its upper bound three. No matrix-block census overlaps our local-algebra samples.
- #4808, head `bd22290761451093aa7aef1fa7b1421627ab0f37`, classifies singular two-role polynomial targets. K[t] is nonlocal. At the shared constant-field boundary its classification assigns cost one to diag(1,0); the fresh literal binary check above gives one as well. Its positive-degree census and our local-algebra samples are different populations.
- #4809, head `6354da68f7a78b9e4db91c796476ae9ebae89a86`, counts invertible targets over F3^4. That nonlocal coefficient algebra and its invertible endpoints differ from this local residue-corank-one theorem; no target count or exact-cost instance overlaps.
- #4810, head `701cb14b7c461253d7ac8243d0722996918bc6c6`, gives the sharp uniform bound for invertible three-role binary field-product targets. Our endpoints have residue corank exactly one, and its sharp coefficient algebra is nonlocal; no target-count or uniform-bound number overlaps.

The other newly opened account PRs #4801/#4803 study Schur spectra/rank pairs, and #4806/#4807 study full-guard probabilities. They do not assert this right-vector factor cost. No discrepancy was found in the stated shared boundary comparison. No predecessor verifier or census was replayed.
